context_requirements: Expression of GPR35 and/or GPR55 or other GPCRs engaged by the antagonist
Constitutive or ligand-driven GPCR signaling contributing to proliferation/survival
Intact downstream PI3K/AKT or MAPK signaling for transcriptional consequences
falsifiers: No consistent transcriptional changes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Changes indistinguishable from vehicle across all lines
Only generic stress/proliferation signatures without any GPCR-related early gene modulation

evidence.supports: Broad-spectrum GPCR antagonist inhibits growth and angiogenesis and increases apoptosis in pancreatic cancer models
GPCR antagonist JTC-801 inhibits proliferation/metastasis and induces apoptosis via PI3K-AKT pathway in ovarian cancer cells
GPCR antagonist pharmacology can be cell-context dependent, supporting variable line responses

changes: No direction changes required: late_up immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IER3, ZFP36, DUSP4/6) are plausibly induced by loss of tonic GPCR signalling, and late_down genes (CCND1, MYC, CXCL2, PTGS2, MMP1, IL1B, EDN1, SERPINE1, TIMP2, CD44) are consistent with reduced GPCR-driven proliferation/inflammation.
No specificity changes required: generic proliferation/stress genes are already placed in generic_effects rather than proximal lists.
No line-response changes required: all lines are scored weak/none, which is compatible with the low-confidence, context-dependent GPCR antagonist mechanism.
No kinetics or magnitude changes required: slow kinetics with weak 6 h and moderate 24 h effects matches the indirect transcriptional consequences of GPCR antagonism.
No evidence changes required: all three cited abstracts support the stated claims.
